messages.text: Liverpool's unwanted record highlights creativity issue

metadata.summary: Liverpool set an unwanted record against Arsenal as they failed to register a shot on target for the first time in 442 Premier League home games, dating back to when records began in 2003.
metadata.content: Liverpool's unwanted record against Arsenal shows creativity problem under Andoni Iraola - Between the Lines | Football News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Analysis Liverpool's unwanted record against Arsenal shows creativity problem under Andoni Iraola - Between the Lines Liverpool suffered a 1-0 loss at Anfield on Sunday as they struggled to break down Arsenal's low block; Andoni Iraola's side have taken the fifth-most shots in the Premier League this season but Between the Lines explains their issues creating high-quality chances By Nick Wright and Adam Smith Tuesday 3 November 2026 17:59, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player We reveal the statistics behind Liverpool's creativity problem Liverpool set an unwanted record against Arsenal as they failed to register a shot on target for the first time in 442 Premier League home games, dating back to when records began in 2003. The ignominious statistic was confirmed by Opta, who initially credited Ronald Araujo and Alexis Mac Allister with shots on target but later ruled them as a blocked shot and overhit pass. Liverpool's finishing was wayward. They were also incorrectly denied a penalty. But a lack of creativity was the bigger issue. Their 17 shots were worth a meagre 1.05 expected goals. It was just the latest example of them struggling to create high-quality chances. messages.text: King's former horse Point Of Law wins Melbourne Cup

metadata.summary: Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington.
metadata.content: Melbourne Cup: Point Of Law storms to Flemington glory for Ciaron Maher | Racing News | Sky Sports Skip to main content Melbourne Cup: Point Of Law storms to Flemington glory for Ciaron Maher Ciaron Maher continued his outstanding recent record in major races, training Point Of Law to Lexus Melbourne Cup glory at Flemington on Tuesday; stablemates Zahrann and Juja Kibo filled the places. Tuesday 3 November 2026 14:11, UK Image: Ethan Brown rides Point Of Law to win the Melbourne Cup (AP Photo/Asanka Brendon Ratnayake) Point Of Law, previously owned by the King and Queen, ran out a decisive winner of a Ciaron Maher dominated Lexus Melbourne Cup in Flemington. Seen as a St Leger hope after finishing fourth in the Queen's Vase at Royal Ascot and winning Newmarket's Bahrain Trophy for former trainers John and Thady Gosden, he was bought privately to continue his career in Australia, winning the Geelong Cup on his first outing for new connections. With stablemate Royal Supremacy setting a strong pace for the big-race favourite to aim at, the son of Frankel showed a deadly turn of foot to run down the eventual fifth as Maher trained not only the first three home but also the fifth and sixth in the 'race that stops the nation'. Maher told Australia's Channel Nine : "I knew I had my best hand going into it, but it's got to execute. I certainly didn't know Royal Supremacy was going to lead by that far but there's nothing better than a true staying test. "Point Of Law has just thrived

messages.text: England's Mitchell ruled out of Nations Championship

metadata.summary: England have been dealt a blow with Alex Mitchell ruled out of the entire Nations Championship after sustaining a hamstring injury during Northampton’s 28-14 victory over Gloucester on Saturday.
metadata.content: England rugby: Alex Mitchell ruled out of entire Nations Championship due to hamstring injury | Rugby Union News | Sky Sports Skip to main content England rugby: Alex Mitchell ruled out of entire Nations Championship due to hamstring injury Alex Mitchell sustained a hamstring injury during Northampton's 28-14 win against Gloucester on Saturday; it is the fourth hamstring injury the scrum-half has sustained this year Tuesday 3 November 2026 16:15, UK Image: Alex Mitchell noaces a prolonged period out of action for club and country. England have been dealt a blow with Alex Mitchell ruled out of the entire Nations Championship after sustaining a hamstring injury during Northampton’s 28-14 victory over Gloucester on Saturday. The British and Irish Lions scrum-half underwent a scan on Monday, with the results confirming he will miss all four of this month's Tests. It is the fourth hamstring injury Mitchell has sustained in 2026, dealing another setback to the scrum-half, who had been expected to play a key role in England's matches against Australia, Japan and New Zealand, as well as the Nations Championship finals weekend from November 27-29.
